libraries.name: Bear
libraries.title: UI components
libraries.description: The flagship React UI kit. Buttons, overlays, inputs, layout, and a theme provider with light and dark mode.

docs.heading: What Bear is
docs.body: Bear is the component layer of ForgeStack. Drop it into a React app, wrap the tree in BearProvider, and the rest of the stack (Grid Table, Rail, forms) can share the same theme tokens.

docs.heading: Install
docs.body: Bear ships its own stylesheet. Import it once next to your app entry.

docs.heading: How it sits in the stack
docs.body: Bear paints the interface. Synapse holds the state those components read. Compass moves between screens. Harbor is the server those screens call. You can use Bear alone.

libraries.name: Rail
libraries.title: Carousels
libraries.description: Touch, snap, loop, and effects for React carousels. Modules stay tree-shakeable.

docs.heading: What Rail is
docs.body: Rail is the motion layer for slides. It is a React carousel you compose from modules instead of one giant config object.

docs.heading: Install
docs.body: Import the package CSS, or copy rail.css into your app if you want to own the stylesheet.

docs.heading: Pair it with Bear
docs.body: Use Bear buttons for next and previous, and Rail for the track. They do not require each other.

libraries.name: Calendar
libraries.title: Events and schedules
libraries.description: Month, week, day, and agenda views for events, with recurrence and an edit surface.
features: Month, week, day, and agenda views

docs.heading: What Calendar is
docs.body: Calendar is the schedule layer. It renders events across month, week, day, and agenda, and keeps recurrence, people, and meeting links on the event itself.

docs.heading: Install
docs.body: Published as @forgedevstack/calendar. Style it with your own tokens or Bear's theme.

docs.heading: Where it connects
docs.body: Harbor can store the events. Forge Query can load them. Bear supplies the dialogs around the grid.

libraries.name: Grid Table
libraries.title: Data grid
libraries.description: Enterprise React grid: range selection, sorting, filtering, pagination, sticky columns, and grouping.

docs.heading: What Grid Table is
docs.body: Grid Table is the dense-data layer. It is built for admin screens: selection that behaves like a spreadsheet, sticky columns, and mobile layouts that still scroll.

docs.heading: Install
docs.body: The package is @forgedevstack/grid-table. The docs on this site cover columns, sorting, filtering, and theming.

docs.heading: How it sits in the stack
docs.body: Feed it rows from Forge Query. Edit cells with Forge Form. Wrap the toolbar in Bear. The grid does not require any of them.

libraries.name: Torch
libraries.title: Media players
libraries.description: Video, audio, reels, and ad players with tracking, playlists, and a sticky mini player.

docs.heading: What Torch is
docs.body: Torch plays video, audio, reels, and ads. Wrap players in TorchProvider when you want one accent, one playlist, and one tracking pipe.

docs.heading: Install
docs.body: Import the stylesheet after your app CSS. Torch's sheet includes layout resets, so load it where you expect that.

docs.heading: A note on the stylesheet
docs.body: TorchPlayer needs a src string. An empty src shows a failed-load state. Point it at a file in public/ or a remote URL.

libraries.name: Synapse
libraries.title: State
libraries.description: Small React state. Nuclei and signals, no dispatch and no reducers. DevTools included.

docs.heading: What Synapse is
docs.body: Synapse replaces a Redux-shaped store with a nucleus you read and write directly. Components subscribe to the slice they pick.

docs.heading: Install
docs.body: No provider is required for a single nucleus. Add the DevTools middleware while you are building.

docs.heading: How it sits in the stack
docs.body: Bear components read Synapse. Forge Query writes server data into a nucleus. Compass guards can read the same auth nucleus.

libraries.name: Forge Form
libraries.title: Forms
libraries.description: Form state and validation, with cache, retries on submit, and a DevTools panel.

docs.heading: What Forge Form is
docs.body: Forge Form keeps field state, validation, and submit next to the inputs. It does not render the inputs. Pair it with Bear fields or your own.

docs.heading: Install
docs.body: The package is framework-light and typed. Validation can be sync or async.

docs.heading: Where the values go
docs.body: On submit, hand the payload to Forge Query or straight to a Harbor route. Synapse can mirror the draft if more than one screen needs it.

libraries.name: Forge Query
libraries.title: Data fetching
libraries.description: Cache, refetch, retry, and dedupe for HTTP. DevTools for the cache.

docs.heading: What Forge Query is
docs.body: Forge Query is the data layer in the browser. It caches responses, retries failed reads, and dedupes the same request from two components.

docs.heading: Install
docs.body: Use it with fetch, or point it at Relay when you want interceptors on the wire.

docs.heading: How it sits in the stack
docs.body: Harbor exposes the routes. Forge Query loads them. Grid Table and Bear render the result. Synapse is optional if you want that data in a nucleus too.

libraries.name: Compass
libraries.title: Routing
libraries.description: Typed client routes with guards, blocked navigation, prefetch, and transitions.
features: Route transitions and a DevTools panel

docs.heading: What Compass is
docs.body: Compass is the client router. Routes are data, guards are functions, and the first paint renders without a refresh when you pass routes into CompassProvider.

docs.heading: Install
docs.body: Use CompassProvider with a routes prop. Guards can be async.

docs.heading: How it sits in the stack
docs.body: Compass decides which Bear screen is visible. Forge Form can block leaving a dirty page. Harbor stays on the server; Compass never replaces it.

libraries.name: Harbor
libraries.title: Node server
libraries.description: A Node framework with routes, controllers, Mongo, auth, websockets, jobs, and cache.

docs.heading: What Harbor is
docs.body: Harbor is the server. You declare routes as functions or as class methods with @route.get and @route.del. A controller calls a service. The CLI can scaffold that shape.

docs.heading: Install
docs.body: The published package is 1.6.x. The bin is harbor. npx @forgedevstack/harbor create scaffolds a starter.

docs.heading: How it sits in the stack
docs.body: Forge Auth plugs into Harbor as middleware. Forge Query calls these routes from the browser. Lingo can localize server messages. Bear never runs here.

libraries.name: Forge Auth
libraries.title: Node auth
libraries.description: HMAC sessions, refresh rotation, cookies, API keys, scrypt, and OIDC with PKCE. This is the Node toolkit, not a React login kit.

docs.heading: What Forge Auth is
docs.body: Forge Auth is server-side auth for Node. It issues sessions, rotates refresh tokens, and exposes Harbor middleware. It is not the React login product.

docs.heading: Install
docs.body: Zero runtime dependencies. Guards are framework-agnostic and the Harbor adapter is included.

docs.heading: How it sits in the stack
docs.body: Harbor mounts the middleware. Compass reads the resulting session on the client and guards routes. Synapse can hold the current user.

libraries.name: Relay
libraries.title: HTTP client
libraries.description: A small fetch client with interceptors, retry, upload progress, and a websocket helper.

docs.heading: What Relay is
docs.body: Relay is the HTTP client. It wraps fetch with interceptors and retry so Forge Query can sit on top, or you can call it directly.

docs.heading: Status
docs.body: Relay is documented here and still settling. Treat the API as early. The land page is the contract we are aiming at.

docs.heading: Install
docs.body: When the package is published, this is the install line.

libraries.name: Kiln
libraries.title: Component docs
libraries.description: A small Storybook-style canvas. kiln init scaffolds it. Stories, search, and a live preview.

docs.heading: What Kiln is
docs.body: Kiln documents components. It is the place Bear stories and your own components get a canvas, a snippet, and a sidebar.

docs.heading: Install
docs.body: kiln init writes kiln.config.json and a first story.

docs.heading: How it sits in the stack
docs.body: Kiln previews Bear, Rail, and Grid Table. It does not ship in your production bundle unless you choose to.

libraries.name: AeroCraft
libraries.title: CSS shortcuts
libraries.description: Short class names compiled to plain CSS with PostCSS. Tokens, breakpoints, and recipes.

docs.heading: What AeroCraft is
docs.body: AeroCraft is a shortcut language that compiles to CSS. You keep tokens in one theme and write short utilities in templates.

docs.heading: Install
docs.body: Use the PostCSS plugin in the app build, or start from the pre-built sheet.

docs.heading: Bear and AeroCraft
docs.body: Bear brings components. AeroCraft brings the utility layer under them. Either one works without the other.

libraries.name: Lingo
libraries.title: i18n
libraries.description: Nested keys, interpolation, CLDR plurals, RTL, and React bindings. Local JSON or a remote bundle.

docs.heading: What Lingo is
docs.body: Lingo translates UI copy. Keys can be nested, plurals follow CLDR, and a provider can set dir and lang for RTL locales.

docs.heading: Install
docs.body: Load JSON bundles locally, or point Lingo at an HTTP source when copy is edited outside the repo.

docs.heading: How it sits in the stack
docs.body: Bear labels, Harbor error messages, and Compass document titles can all read from one Lingo catalog.

libraries.name: Anvil
libraries.title: Utilities and hooks
libraries.description: Typed helpers and React hooks: clone, guards, debounce, and collection utilities. Tree-shakeable.

docs.heading: What Anvil is
docs.body: Anvil is the utility belt. Import the one function you need. Nothing else ships in the bundle.

docs.heading: Install
docs.body: Works in React, Vue, and plain TypeScript. Hooks live on a separate entry so Vue apps do not pull React.

docs.heading: How it sits in the stack
docs.body: Every other library can call Anvil. Your app can too. It does not own state, routing, or UI.

tools.name: Forge CLI
tools.title: Project scaffolding
tools.description: npx scaffolder for React, server, and full-stack ForgeStack apps. Templates, Bear, and a Synapse generator.

docs.heading: What the CLI is
docs.body: Forge CLI creates a project that already points at the libraries you pick. It is a tool, not a runtime dependency of your app.

docs.heading: Create a project
docs.body: Choose a template, a package manager, and whether Bear should be included. Harbor has its own create command for a server starter.

docs.heading: Harbor starter
docs.body: For a Harbor API, use the Harbor package bin. It prints the ForgeStack mark and scaffolds route, controller, and service.

extensions.name: GitForge
extensions.title: Git for VS Code and Cursor
extensions.description: Git actions from the editor sidebar. Built for VS Code and Cursor.
features: Git actions without leaving the editor

docs.heading: What GitForge is
docs.body: GitForge is the editor extension for Git. It is not an npm library. Install the VSIX from Open VSX into VS Code or Cursor.

docs.heading: Install
docs.body: Or open the Open VSX page and install from there. The button on this page goes to that listing.

docs.heading: Why it is in the stack
docs.body: ForgeStack covers the app and the editor you build it in. GitForge is that editor piece. LintForge sits next to it for style rules.

extensions.name: LintForge
extensions.title: Style rules in the editor
extensions.description: Editor enforcement for ForgeStack style: types in type files, constants in const files.

docs.heading: What LintForge is
docs.body: LintForge is the editor extension for project style. The npm rule package is still landing. The VSIX is what you install today.

docs.heading: Install
docs.body: Open VSX is the listing. Use it in VS Code or Cursor beside GitForge.

docs.heading: What it checks
docs.body: Keep types in type files and constants in const files, and keep Bear UI code on the same layout as the rest of the stack.
